### Changed
- **The Substrate pin moves to `0.0.27-gs.5`** (`components.substrate` and `components.substrate-crds` floor, the customer BOM, `kagent.substrateWorkerPool.workerImage`): gs.3 plus a golden boot whose image the registry refuses failing instead of resuming forever (gs.4, giantswarm/substrate#14 — giantswarm/giantswarm#37742 row 27) and the `podcertificate-controller-system` namespace kept across an uninstall (gs.5, giantswarm/substrate#13 — #384).
### Fixed
- **A reinstall after `helm uninstall` brings Agent Substrate up with a consistent trust chain** (giantswarm/agent-platform#384). The uninstall took the `podcertificate-controller-system` namespace and the two CA pools in it with the `substrate` release while the signers' cluster-scoped `ClusterTrustBundle`s stayed; the reinstall minted new roots and the podcertificate-controller republished the bundles within seconds, but every Substrate pod had projected the surviving bundle when it started and reads its CA once, at dial time — `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` against ate-api-server from ate-controller, atelet and the atenet router, no golden boot (the own-Flux ATS scenario on the cluster the smoke had uninstalled from, PR #380). Two halves: the Substrate line keeps the namespace across an uninstall (`helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`, 0.0.27-gs.5, giantswarm/substrate#13 — the pin below), and the connectivity bootstrap hook publishes both signers' `ClusterTrustBundle`s from the pools (server-side, the way it applies `actor-id-ca-certs`) before the `substrate` release installs and on every upgrade, so a bundle never reaches a pod with roots its pool does not have; the hook's ClusterRole gains `clustertrustbundles` (get, list, watch, create, patch) and `attest` on the two podcert signers (the apiserver admits a bundle that names a signer only from a client allowed to attest it). The ATS smoke no longer removes Substrate's leftovers between its scenarios: the own-Flux scenario reinstalls onto the cluster the smoke uninstalled from — the kept namespace, pools and bundles in place — and asserts each signer's bundle carries its pool's roots; the smoke asserts what the uninstall leaves.
